page: Microsoft Azure D48pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V, utilizing the ARM64 architecture with 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs. Powered by the 3.4 GHz Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor, the instance operates with 1 thread per core and features 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 128 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 192.0 GB of RAM, offering an even 4.0 GB per core. The server includes 2832 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and operates without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and memory subsystems. Geekbench multi-core reaches 22118.0 and stress-ng multi-core reaches 99348.93, both placing in the upper tiers. Memory bandwidth is notably high, achieving 463.49 GB/sec read and 198.92 GB/sec write on large uncached blocks, complemented by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3334.28. Database operations and in-memory key-value processing are strong, highlighted by 89.81 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 36588.41 in PassMark database operations. Conversely, single-core metrics remain average, with Geekbench single-core at 1704.0 and stress-ng single-core at 2075.08. Large LLM generation speeds also remain low without hardware acceleration.

The dedicated physical core architecture provides predictable throughput and resource efficiency for multi-threaded applications, supported by large local NVMe storage for transient data needs. However, software requiring x86-specific instruction sets like AVX-512 or heavy per-thread clock gains will face tradeoffs. Microsoft Azure D48pds_v6 is well suited for relational databases, Redis caching layers, multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving clusters, and containerized enterprise microservices.
description: Microsoft Azure D48pds_v6 is a general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 48 dedicated ARM64 Neoverse-N2 cores running at 3.4 GHz without multithreading. It features 192.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB per core, along with 2832 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and no GPU hardware. The server delivers top-tier memory bandwidth, reaching 463.49 GB/sec read and 198.92 GB/sec write on uncached blocks, alongside strong Geekbench multi-core scores and high PassMark database operational metrics. Single-thread processing performs at average levels, making the architecture reliant on core parallelism. With its fast local disk and dedicated processor design, the instance offers strong resource density for distributed databases, high-throughput caching systems, static web infrastructure, and continuous integration compilation pipelines.
